source.title: All Code, No Thought: Current Language Models Struggle to Reason in Ciphered Language
source.authors: Shiyuan Guo; Henry Sleight; Fabien Roger

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports scaling of ciphered-reasoning task accuracy during fine-tuning, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Its result concerns a related but different outcome, so it does not test a listed version of the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper's Section 5.2 reports fine-tuning-token scaling for ciphered-reasoning accuracy and translation BLEU. These are not held-out pretraining loss measurements; it also does not fit or test a compute-optimal parameter/token split. The ciphered-reasoning accuracy result is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The paper studies whether LLMs can reason in ciphered text. Its 'scaling laws' (Section 5.2, Figures 6, 8-10) are plots of MATH500 task accuracy and translation BLEU against fine-tuning tokens for Qwen2.5 3B/7B/14B, with no power-law fit, no held-out loss and no compute-optimal analysis. It uses 'scaling laws' loosely and neither tests nor relies on the listed versions. The record's 'discusses' overstates the link; at most the term is borrowed, so cites_only/T6.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance, but incomplete. The authors' main conclusion is that models struggle to reason in ciphered text despite translating it well, so ciphered reasoning is an unlikely way to evade CoT monitoring today. The scaling result (slow gains, 14B still below unciphered at 3.7B tokens) is a secondary finding.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales fine-tuning data for ciphered-reasoning task accuracy rather than measuring pretraining loss or compute-optimal allocation.

fits_no_version.finding: Ciphered-reasoning accuracy rises slowly with fine-tuning tokens (letter to word with dot, up to 3.7B tokens). Qwen2.5 14B stays below unciphered accuracy; larger models do better. Translation BLEU saturates by about 125M tokens for 7B/14B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning data needed to learn reasoning in an unfamiliar encoding greatly exceeds that needed to learn to translate it, and accuracy grows slowly with data and model size.

record.problems: For the related scaling result, the paper reports one cipher and does not provide a fitted power law or uncertainty estimates. It does not measure the loss quantity in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. Other scaling plots and translation results do not measure the held-out pretraining loss or compute-optimal allocation named in the claim.

untested.parts: All: no held-out pretraining loss measured.
All: no extrapolation from small-run fits.
All: fine-tuning accuracy is plotted against tokens but no power-law form is fitted or tested for loss.
All: downstream accuracy is not related to pretraining loss or to pretraining scale under any fit. Only fine-tuning data and three model sizes are varied for one cipher.

record.verdict_notes: Off-topic for scaling_laws: the term 'scaling laws' refers to unfitted accuracy-vs-fine-tuning-token curves. Figure 7 and Table 7 show larger Qwen models do better on ciphers, but this is a task-accuracy comparison across three sizes with no fit, so no version applies.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute was not measured.
The paper does not test whether small-run loss fits predict larger-run loss.
It does not compare parameter/token allocations at fixed compute or fit their growth with compute.
It does not compare architecture details at a fixed parameter count.
It studies fine-tuning-token scaling of ciphered-reasoning accuracy, not whether the same power-law form holds for held-out loss in fine-tuning or other regimes.
It does not test downstream performance scaling with pretraining loss.
It does not test how exponents or compute-optimal splits depend on setup or fitting choices, or whether loss curves depart from a power law.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5 14B
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned on increasing quantities of data encoded in the letter-to-word-with-dot cipher; evaluated ciphered-reasoning accuracy.
rows.measure: MATH 500 ciphered-reasoning accuracy (adherent and correct responses)
rows.value: At 3.7B tokens, it still cannot match the unciphered model's accuracy.
rows.note: The authors state that reasoning capability improves slowly with more data but remains below the unciphered model at 3.7B tokens. This is task accuracy, not held-out cross-entropy loss.
rows.check: The row measures ciphered-reasoning MATH500 accuracy against fine-tuning tokens, not held-out pretraining loss, so it bears on no version. The 'partial' state was judged against the unciphered baseline, not against any version's effect, so it is cannot_determine for the claim. The row may be kept as a fits_no_version record.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
